basics.name: Gaohan Ye
basics.label: Hardware Engineer: DFT, Design Verification, and Computer Architecture
basics.summary: M.S. in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, with industry experience in DFT at Astera Labs and design verification at Rivian Automotive. Published researcher in computer architecture and LLM acceleration (IEEE CAL Best Paper Award, HPCA 2026).

work.name: Astera Labs
work.position: DFT Engineer Intern, Leo CXL Memory Controller
work.summary: Design-for-test engineering for the Leo CXL Memory Controller: memory BIST insertion, ATPG, boundary scan, and test-pattern automation.
highlights: Inserted Synopsys STAR Memory System (SMS) BIST/repair into 3 blocks covering 186 SRAM macros in 9 vendor configurations
Debugged transition-delay (TDF) ATPG failures on I3C/I2C logic and wrote false-path constraints to close uncovered timing paths
Root-caused MBIST and boundary-scan gate-level simulation failures across DDR4 and DDR5 configurations
Built two Python toolchains (~4,000 lines) with byte-exact regression checks, automating die-to-package pin remapping of boundary-scan BSDL and ATE STIL patterns
Verified converted patterns end-to-end with Slurm-dispatched VCS gate-level simulation, debugging failures in Verdi
Generated block-level stuck-at ATPG patterns and ported them to a top-level testbench: 205 patterns, 0 mismatches

work.name: Rivian Automotive
work.position: Design Verification Intern, RAP1 Silicon Team
work.summary: Developed system-level testcases for RAP1 (Rivian Autonomy Processor), a custom 5nm AI inference chip delivering 1600 sparse TOPS for autonomous driving compute.
highlights: Developed system-level testcases for RAP1 (Rivian Autonomy Processor), a custom 5nm AI inference chip delivering 1600 sparse TOPS for autonomous driving compute
Increased toggle coverage to over 90% via a new, more efficient coverage generation flow
Enhanced an existing integration test suite, reducing the failure rate from over 40% to less than 5%
Developed a new system-level test to validate memory access, creating a baseline for future verification tests
Authored new FuSa tests to validate error injection and interrupt mechanisms for critical components

work.name: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
work.position: Teaching Assistant for Digital Systems Laboratory, ECE 385
work.summary: Teaching assistant for digital systems laboratory course covering FPGA and microprocessor implementations.
highlights: Evaluated SystemVerilog/FPGA projects and microprocessor system implementations
Conducted technical demonstrations and assessments of digital circuits, state machines, and SoC designs
Graded lab reports covering combinational/sequential logic, timing analysis, and hardware-software co-design

work.name: Rivian Automotive
work.position: Design Verification Intern, RAP1 Silicon Team
work.summary: Developed verification infrastructure and performance monitoring for RAP1 automotive chip designs.
highlights: Created performance monitor to track AXI transaction signals to test read and write operation performance
Increased toggle coverage of chip blocks by creating and implementing new targeted tests
Conducted system-level verification for the DUT using a custom UVM testbench
Developed and executed detailed test plans, identifying bugs and successfully debugging and resolving issues

Offered comprehensive support to students, addressing inquiries regarding x86, virtual memory, scheduling, file systems, and course materials
Graded over 300 student assignments and conducted demos of their custom operating systems
Collaborated with professors in the grading process for midterms and final exams

publications.name: Transparent Memory Management for Large-Scale LLM Training and Tuning
publications.summary: Characterized LLM training memory-access patterns, revealing strong spatial and cross-iteration temporal locality in large tensor accesses. These findings motivated transparent UVM-based CPU-memory offloading with a coalescing prefetcher to relieve network bottlenecks in distributed training. Advisor: Prof. Nam Sung Kim.

publications.name: ReScue: Reliable and secure CXL memory
publications.publisher: IEEE International Symposium on High-Performance Computer Architecture (HPCA)
publications.summary: Co-authored paper on reliable and secure CXL memory with Chihun Song, Austin Antony Cruz, Michael Jaemin Kim, Minbok Wi, Kyungsan Kim, Sangyeol Lee, Jung Ho Ahn, and Nam Sung Kim. Presented at HPCA 2026.

publications.name: Exploiting Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for LLM Inference
publications.summary: Characterized Intel AMX GEMM/GEMV throughput on a dual-socket Sapphire Rapids server across OPT-125M to OPT-175B matrix shapes, establishing the CPU performance profile behind an arithmetic-intensity-based CPU-GPU partitioning policy. The system achieved 12.1x lower latency and 2.2x higher throughput than GPU-only OPT-30B inference. Advisor: Prof. Nam Sung Kim. Received IEEE Best Paper Award.

projects.name: VLSI Physical Design
projects.summary: Took a custom datapath from transistor-level cells to routed layout in FreePDK45 using Cadence Virtuoso, Innovus, and Synopsys Design Compiler (ECE course).
highlights: Built an area-optimized custom CMOS standard cell library, verified via DRC, LVS, and digital simulation
Designed schematic and physical layout of a bit-sliced datapath with a custom ALU and register file
Optimized CMOS transistor sizing to balance strict area constraints with worst-case pull-up/pull-down drive strength
Ran Design Compiler synthesis and Innovus place-and-route, taking RTL to routed layout

projects.name: NPU-CPU LLM Inference
projects.summary: Led an ECE 527 project modeling Llama 3.1 8B inference split across a Furiosa RNGD NPU and an Intel AMX CPU.
highlights: Designed an analytical performance model partitioning inference by arithmetic intensity and batch size, predicting end-to-end latency from measured component latencies
Derived three batch-size-adaptive policies; hybrid NPU prefill + CPU decode showed 12% average latency overhead vs. H100 at 2.6x lower system power
Projected 23-40% lower three-year total cost of ownership than H100-based systems

projects.name: Multi-stage RISC-V Processor
projects.summary: Designed and implemented RV32I processor in SystemVerilog with data & branch hazard detection as team project.
highlights: Achieved 28.6% frequency increase and 47% cache stall reduction
Secured 3rd place among 30 groups
Applied timing analysis and logic optimization principles for hardware-software co-design

projects.name: Linux Kernel
projects.summary: Built a custom Linux Kernel featuring 3 terminals and 6 processes with essential OS features.
highlights: Implemented read-only File System, Round-Robin Scheduling, 4kB and 4MB Paging
Successfully handled interrupts, exceptions, and system calls from user programs
Developed complete kernel from scratch using C and x86 assembly

projects.name: FPGA Flappy Bird Game
projects.summary: Developed a complete Flappy Bird game implementation on FPGA using SystemVerilog, Python, and C.
highlights: Programmed an FPGA to output a VGA signal to draw game visuals to a monitor
Enabled keyboard-FPGA communication via SPI to run C-based keyboard drivers on SoC
Wrote Python scripts to compress PNG format into MIF format to instantiate onto the FPGA on-chip memory
Implemented state machine in SystemVerilog to animate a walking character depending on keyboard inputs
Detected collisions between the map and the player with state machine-controlled memory address into ROMs
